caseno: Civil Petition for Leave to Appeal No. 1923 of 2011.
lawyer:
ABM Bayzid, Advocate instructed by Syed Mahbubar Rahman Advocate-on-Record-----For Petitioners. 

Mahmudul Islam, Senior Advocate instructed by Mr Md Ziaul Abedin Advocate-on-Record-----For the Respondent No. 1. 

None Represented-----For the Respondent Nos. 2-3.
parties:
University Grants Commission and another ----- Petitioners 
Vs
University of Information Technology & Science and another  ----- Respondents
full_judgment:
2. Respondent No. 1 herein as writ-petitioner (hereinafter referred . to as the petitioner) filed the above mentioned writ petition before the High Court Division challenging the decision of the University Grants Commission shutting down its outer campuses at Rajshahi and Chittagong vide Memo No. বিমক/বেঃবিঃ/জি-১৫/৪৩১(২)/০৩/৬৬৮৯ Dated 25-10-2009 issued under the signature of the Director, Private University Division to have been issued without lawful authority and also praying for direction upon the respondents to give approval to its outer campuses at the said two places. Rule was issued in the terms as prayed for. At the time of issuing the Rule, operation of the impugned Memo dated 25-10-2009 was stayed. 

 3. The case of the petitioner as made out in the writ petition, inter-alia, was that it was established on 7-8-2003, vide Education Ministry's Memo No. বিমক/বেঃ বিঃ/জি-১৫/৪৩১(২)/০৩/৬৬৮৯ through provisional approval of the Government. After proper Enquiry and investigation, the writ-respondents granted provisional approval to the petitioner and thereafter, the writ-respondents granted permission to admit students after 7-8-2003. The petitioner admitted 7,894 students who are now in various stages of their education and currently there are 217 faculty members. The first convocation of the petitioner-University was held on 20-7-2009 wherein the chancellor of the University, the Hon'ble President of the People's Republic of Bangladesh was present. Dr APJ Abdul Kalam, former Hon'ble President of India was the convocation speaker in that ceremony. Dr Gowher Rizvi, Adviser to the Prime Minister of Bangladesh on Foreign affairs, was present as special guest. The petitioner started its operation at the provisional site in accordance with the condition of approval letter dated 7-8-2003. Due to increase in number of students, the petitioner had to increase number of campuses in and outside of Dhaka. Outside Dhaka, campuses, such as Rajshahi and Chittagong are functioning. According to section 4 of the Private Universities Act, 1992 (the Act, 1992) a University may be situated in any part of Bangladesh. As there is nothing in the Act, 1992 regarding setting up of campuses in other places than its original place of establishment, respondent No. 1 took decision on 31-12-2001 vide Memo No. সিম/শাঃ ১৪/৮ বেঃ বিঃ -৮/২০০০/৬৩২(২৭)that Universities may inform concerned authority and can open outer campuses after the University is in operation at its approved original place of campus. The outer campuses must have sufficient number of qualified teachers and infrastructure for facility and classroom in the proposed outer campus. The petitioner-University was initially permitted at Gulshan Campus but due to increase of number of students and programs in different campuses, it had to take new building. Having regard to the existing law, the petitioner informed and sought permission from the authorities to run programs at these campuses. However, none of these applications have been approved till date. The petitioner applied for approval of its Rajshahi campus on 2 April, 2006 and Chittagong campus on 26 April 2007. The requirements for application were fulfilled as per law. The law requires that a Private University should have 5 acres of land (2,16,000 square feet). As it is now impossible to find this quantum of land in any urban area almost all Private Universities are operative in multi-storied buildings and the petitioner's buildings have 2,25,000 square feet of floor space. All the Universities which have been approved are also based on the floor space calculation. The floor space of Chittagong campus is 44,000 square feet and Rajshahi campus is 27,000 square feet. At present the academic activities are being conducted in three buildings in Dhaka and two buildings at Chittagong and three buildings at Rajshahi. There are 11 computer labs, 3 physics laboratories, 3 Mechanics laboratories, 3 Telecommunication laboratories, 3 Chemistry laboratories, 3 Electronic Circuit laboratories, 3 Microprocessor laboratories, 6 Libraries having 25 thousand books, 500 journals/periodicals and 75 class rooms in the said buildings. All class rooms, Library, labs are air conditioned and well equipped in all respects. The petitioner informed the respondents by letters dated the 2nd April, 2006 and the 26th April, 2007 that the academic activities were being expanded in outer campuses following all terms and conditions of the provisional approval. Its campuses would be built at Rajshahi and Chittagong and for that, 43 acres of land have been purchased at Rajshahi and 1.96 acres of land have been purchased at Chittagong. Construction of Chittagong campus building is now complete. The construction work has begun at Rajshahi. Therefore, the petitioner established the approved principal campus in Dhaka. The campuses at Rajshahi and Chittagong have been established having regard to the requirements of the respondents. In accordance with the above mentioned decision, the petitioner applied for the approval of these two campuses on 16-5-2006 and 26-4-2007 respectively. The applications were not approved, which was informed vide letter dated 15-5-2007, on the ground that the Private University Ordinance, 2007 was in progress and at its final stage and the decision on the applications would be taken after the Ordinance was enacted. The petitioner has fulfilled the requirements of the respondents inasmuch as the buildings have 226000 square feet of floor space against the requirements of 5 acres of land. Each faculty requires 1 professor and 13 lectures. At present, the petitioner-University has 3 faculties (School Engineering, Liberal Arts, Business) and 32 professors, 23 Associate Professors and 162 lectures are working in the various faculties. Respondent No. 1, under the signature of respondent No. 3 issued show cause notice vide Memo dated 30-9-2009 asking the petitioner to explain within 7 (seven) days regarding the said outer campuses and publication of advertisement with the photograph of the Hon'ble President and Chancellor. On receipt of the said notice, the petitioner prayed for 2 (two) months' time to respondent No. 1 to give reply and respondent No. 1 allowed one month's time vide letter dated 26-10-2009. Meantime respondent No. 2, the University Grants Commission issued the impugned Memo directing the petitioner to shut down its outer campuses at Rajshahi and Chittagong and to explain as to why the petitioner was continuing admission of students in the said outer campuses. In the Memo the petitioner was also asked not to admit students in the unapproved programme of B.Sc. in Civil Engineering. Then the petitioner filed the writ petition and obtained the Rule on 3-11-2009 in the terms as already stated hereinbefore. 

 4. The petitioner filed 3 (three) supplementary affidavits in support of the writ petition. In the first supplementary affidavit filed on 6-1-2010 it was stated, inter-alia, that while passing the Order of stay for a period of 2 (two) months at the time of issuing the Rule on 3-11-2009, it was mentioned that no further extension would be given unless the petitioner could produce paper to show that approval was given for running outer campuses. In the above context, the Registrar of the petitioner-University made further applications to respondent No. 1 on 19-11-2009 and 4-1-2010 for giving approval for running outer campuses of the University showing the reasons but respondent No. 1 did not make any response to the said applications. The said two outer campuses were being run with full facilities and requirements as required by the respondents. 6 (six) thousand students had already been admitted to those 2 (two) outer campuses and in the present semester 1 (one) thousand students have been admitted. 

 5. In the second supplementary affidavit filed on 23-2-2011, it was stated, inter-alia, that in reply to the further applications filed to respondent No. 1 for giving approval for running the campuses of the petitioner at Chittagong and Rajshahi, respondent No. 2 issued letters for inspection of the campuses of the petitioner at Rajshahi and Chittagong on 22-12-2010, 27-12-2010 and 29-12-2010. After inspection, respondent No. 2 issued further letter on 13-1-2011 to the petitioner requiring it to fulfill some requirements for getting approval of the said 2 (two) campuses. 

 6. In the third supplementary affidavit filed on 13-3-2011 it was stated that on 27-12-2010 the petitioner deposited Taka 1,00,000 (50,000 + 50,000), by two payment Orders separately for inspection of its campuses at Rajshahi and Chittagong on 4-1-2011, 6-1-2011 and 27-2-2011. After completion of the inspection of the 2 (two) campuses by a team of respondent No. 2, the petitioner submitted 2 (two) applications to respondent No. 2 to give copy of the inspection report and the progress of the approval of its 2 (two) campuses at Rajshahi and Chittagong but till date the concerned respondents did not make any response to the applications of the petitioner. In the affidavit, the petitioner further contended that according to section 3 (5) of the Banla??? (the Ain, 2010) a University can open any independent campuses or Universities in any part of the country in similar name. The petitioner has acquired vested right and legitimate expectation to continue its educational activities in its campuses at Rajshahi and Chittagong and is also entitled to get direction upon the respondents to give approval to the campuses at Rajshahi and Chittagong as it already complied with the conditions provided in the Ain, 2010. The petitioner filed another application on 24-1-2010 addressing the Director (in charge) Private University Division of the University Grants Commission along with to give approval to the campuses at Rajshahi and Chittagong but in spite of several reminders, the respondents have not given approval to those campuses. In view of the inaction of the respondents several thousand students belonging to middle class family along with the teachers and the staffs are spending their days in uncertainty. 

 7. Writ-respondent No. 2, the University Grants Commission (petitioner No. 1 herein) filed an affidavit-in-opposition to contest the Rule contending, inter-alia, that the petitioner University received Government approval provisionally under the provisions of the Act, 1992 as amended in 1998 on the condition that within 5 (five) years the proposed University shall have its permanent campus in 5 acres of land with sufficient infrastructure and start its curriculum with the approval from the University Grants Commission. The Ministry of Education vide its Memo No. শিম/সাঃ ১৪/৮ বেঃ বিঃ ৮/২০০০/৬৩২(২৭)Dated 31-12-2001 allowed 26 Private Universities to open outer campuses for extension of their education programs maintaining the standard of education fulfilling the condition that without the approval of the Government no outer campuses "would" be started in each faculty/department and there must be approval from the University Grants Commission about the education programme of the outer campuses for each faculty and there must be sufficient infrastructure. The petitioner-University was not in the list because of the fact that it was established on 7-8-2003. The Officers of University Grants Commission did not inspect outer campuses of the Private Universities because the concerned Universities did not take any initiative for holding such Enquiry. The outer campuses of the petitioner were not at all approval by the Government. Moreover, the Memo No. শিম/সাঃ ১৭/৮ বাঃ বিঃ ৮/২০০০/৬৩২(২৭) dated 31-12-2001 was cancelled by Memo No. শিম/সাঃ ১৭/৮ বাঃ বিঃ ৮/২০০০/৬৩২ (৫৫) dated 25-6-2007 and it was informed to all 52 Private Universities of Bangladesh. The  petitioner before fulfilling the conditions as contained in the Act, 1992 opened its outer campuses unauthorized and as such, its prayer was not approved by the concerned authority. The petitioner fulfilled the requirements to establish the University of Information, Technology and Science only and not for its outer campuses. The petitioner from the very beginning did not obtain any permission to open outer campuses and also publish photograph of the Hon'ble President of the People's Republic of Bangladesh and the former Hon'ble President of India in their advertisement for admission of students, such advertisement was against decency. The petitioner did not submit any reply to the notice as mentioned in Annexure-'1' to the writ petition in spite of extension of time. Since the petitioner did not obtain permission, the respondents had no other alternative but to stop the outer campuses and the impugned Order was served rightly. The petitioner opened outer campuses at Rajshahi and Chittagong unauthorized disregarding the law and the decision issued by the concerned authority. In spite of the impugned letter dated 25-10-2010 issued by respondent No. 2 the petitioner did not stop its outer campuses and has been running those without approval of the concerned authority. In the present Ain, there is no provision for outer campuses of a Private University, so all the Private Universities have been directed by the Government and the University Grants Commission to close down their outer campuses with immediate effect. The petitioner-University is not legally entitled to start and run the outer campuses inasmuch as it did not take any approval from the Government to start and continue its outer campuses at different places of Bangladesh. 

 10. Mr. ABM Bayzid, learned Advocate, appearing for the petitioners, has contended that the learned Judges of the High Court Division erred in law in giving direction upon the respondents to consider the case of the petitioner with regard to opening of the independent campuses at Chittagong and Rajshahi inasmuch as in the present law, the Ain, 2010 which was promulgated on 18th July, 2010 there is no provision for opening outer campuses outside the main University campus. In support of his submission, he has specifically referred to sub-section (5) of section 3 of the Ain, 2010 explaining that the sub-section only permits the existing Private University to establish a new University in the same name or synonymous name with the approval of the Government and fulfilling the other requirements as mandated in the Ain, but the petitioner did not apply for establishing such University, rather applied for approval of establishment of its outer campuses at Rajshahi and Chittagong. Therefore, the University Grants Commission did not rightly act on the applications filed by the petitioner. He has further contended that by giving life to the Order of stay "granted earlier", that is, at the time of issuing Rule and thereafter extended till the appropriate decision is taken by the respondents including the University Grants Commission, the High Court Division in fact has allowed the petitioner-University to carry on with its academic activities in the unauthorized outer campuses at Rajshahi and Chittagong and thus made the provisions of the Ain, 2010 ineffective and as such, the impugned judgment and Order calls for interference by this Court by way of granting leave. 

 11. Mr. Mahmudul Islam, learned Counsel, entering caveat on behalf of the writ petitioner-respondent No. 1, on the other hand, has supported the impugned judgment and Order. He by referring to Annexures-'Q' and 'R' series Annexed to the supplementary affidavit dated 23-2-2011 has submitted that from the said Annexures, it is clear that the petitioner fulfilled all the requirements as mandated in the Ain, 2010, that is, it filed the Trust deed, made deposit of the required money for opening the outer campuses at Rajshahi and Chittagong and submitted the lease deeds showing taking of lease of the spaces for those two outer campuses, the respondents were under obligation to allow the academic activities at those outer campuses, instead they sat over the matter and then gave the direction to the petitioner to shut down those outer campuses, the High Court Division rightly gave the direction upon the respondents to consider the applications of the petitioner for giving approval of its outer campuses at Chittagong and Rajshahi, so no interference is called for by this Division with the impugned judgment and Order and the leave petition be dismissed. 

 13. From the statements of the writ petition as well as the supplementary affidavit, it appears that the whole grievance of the petitioner is that though it fulfilled all the criteria to open independent outer campuses at Chittagong and Rajshahi, its applications for giving approval to the said outer campuses were not disposed of till filing of the writ petition, not only that by the impugned memo it was asked to shut down those two outer campuses which compelled it to file the writ petition, whereas writ-respondent No. 2's case is that there being no provision in the Ain, 2010 to open any outer campuses outside the permanent seat of a Private University, the petitioner is not entitled to get approval of its two outer campuses at Rajshahi and Chittagong, so it did not rightly consider its case to give approval to its said outer campuses. The University Grants Commission has not denied the fact that the petitioner filed applications for giving approval to open outer campuses at Chittagong and Rajshahi. It is also a fact that till date such applications filed by the petitioner have not been disposed of by the respondents in either way. The petitioner has claimed that it has fulfilled all the criteria as mandated in the Ain, 2010 to get approval for opening independent outer campuses at Chittagong and Rajshahi. 

 14. On perusal of the various provisions of the Ain, 2010 particularly sections 3,6,7 and 13, it appears that it is the Government and the University Grants Commission which enjoy the exclusive domain to give approval for the establishment of the Private University at any place in Bangladesh and whether in exercise of their power under the provisions of the Ain, 2010, they can accord permission for establishing independent outer campuses is a matter to be decided by them and since the said two authorities have not taken any decision in the matter, we do not consider it proper and advisable to make any comment of our own in the matter, because such comment may jeopardize the discretion given to exercise of power by the said two statutory authorities under the Ain, 2010. We are of the view that writ-respondent Nos. 1 and 2 should be allowed to exercise their wisdom in taking decision on the prayer made by the petitioner for establishing outer campuses at Chittagong and Rajshahi in accordance with the provisions of the Ain, 2010 without any interference by this Court. At the same time, we do not approve of the action of the respondents in sitting over the applications of the petitioner so long they had every right to decide the applications in either way. In the context, we find the observations made by the High Court Division that in the meantime, the petitioner has fulfilled the criteria and also complied with the conditions as mandated in proviso to section 3 (5) and sub-section (9) of section 6 of the Ain, 2010 and as such, it is entitled to have "permission of independent campus of Rajshahi and Chittagong" indiscreet. When the High Court Division gave direction upon the writ-respondents to consider the case of the petitioner with regard to the opening of independent campuses at Chittagong and Rajshahi in accordance with law, it should not have made any comment as to merit to the entitlement of the petitioner to get approval of establishing the outer campuses at Rajshahi and Chittagong. Furthermore, when the learned Advocate for the petitioner did not press the first part of the Rule as to the shutting down of the outer campuses and as per own statements of the petitioner approval to establish outer campuses of the University at Rajshahi and Chittagong was not given by the concerned writ-respondents, the High Court Division was totally wrong in allowing the Order of stay of operation of the impugned Order passed earlier to continue till the appropriate decision is taken by the respondents, because by such Order of stay in fact the petitioner has been allowed to continue with its academic activities in the unapproved campuses at Rajshahi and Chittagong nullifying the impugned Order as well as the provisions of the Ain, 2010. 

 (b) The writ-respondents are directed to dispose of the applications filed by the petitioner for giving approval to its outer campuses at Rajshahi and Chittagong in accordance with the provisions of the বেসরকারী 	বিশ্ববিদ্যালয় আইন, ২০১০ within 2 (two) months from date.
